content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (INDEMN), fallback-level cure.**

- **Investigated:** Subparagraph 21.2 (reciprocal owner-liability indemnity, Schedule B share cap), Paragraph 32.1–32.6 (pro rata reimbursement, notice to Management Committee, settlement control, survival on termination), Paragraph 21.3 (mutual consequential-loss exclusion), plus targeted searches for indemnify / infringe / licence / patent / royalty — no IP-infringement indemnity exists anywhere.
- **Classification:** The multilateral cost-sharing structure fails the fallback on a material term (no supplier-side IP indemnity, no procure/modify/replace or refund remedies), so a redline was warranted.
- **Cure:** One insertion (new Subparagraph 32.7, after 32.6) carrying only the seven fallback elements — IP indemnity in our favour, modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure-modify-replace, refund, and the 3× annual charges super-cap. Preferred was not pursued because narrowing our own reciprocal 21.2 indemnity would require collateral rewrites of the consortium's Schedule B sharing mechanic.
